about: The code examples of the chapter 1 deck, in the order of the code slides (order = slide order). The page's chapter-code tab lists them by NAME in this order; every example is self-contained and runs with Python's built-in functions and the standard-library module math (no keyboard input: where the book calls input(), the example names the text input() would return); the expected result is what the run printed. The code is exactly the text of the deck's code boxes with the '>>> ' prompt removed; a line that is meant to fail sits in a two-line try/except so that the error text is part of the result.

page_requirements: Python built-ins: print, type, len, str, int, float, round, repr, bin, format; the standard-library module math (import math); the try/except statement; no keyboard input

examples.name: Your first program
examples.code:
print('Hello, world!')
print('What is your name?')
my_name = 'Ayse'  # the text input() would return
print('It is good to meet you, ' + my_name)
print('The length of your name is:')
print(len(my_name))
my_age = '20'  # input() returns text
next_age = int(my_age) + 1
print('You will be ' + str(next_age) + ' next year.')
examples.expected:
Hello, world!
What is your name?
It is good to meet you, Ayse
The length of your name is:
4
You will be 21 next year.

examples.name: Dissecting the program
examples.code:
name = 'Alice'
age = 20
print('Hello, ' + name + '! You are ' + str(age) + '.')
print(f'Hello, {name}! You are {age}.')
examples.expected:
Hello, Alice! You are 20.
Hello, Alice! You are 20.
